ai.description: Nanorana parkeri is a small frog (30–45 mm) with a grey-brown dorsum and dark mottling. It features a distinct, rounded snout and prominent skin folds along the flanks. It lacks vomerine teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana parkeri* is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, black-tipped glandular warts scattered across its back, which are absent in similar sympatric species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana parkeri* inhabits high-altitude alpine meadows and streams in the Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 3,500 and 4,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Nanorana parkeri* is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates near high-altitude streams and rocky pools in the Himalayas.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana parkeri* is an oviparous frog that breeds from June to August. Females lay small clutches of eggs in high-altitude streams or pools.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana parkeri* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh in the Indian Himalayas, typically occurring at elevations between 3,000 and 4,500m.
ai.callDescription: The High Himalaya Frog emits a series of short, low-pitched, pulsed notes while submerged in cold, high-altitude streams.
